metadata.title: Global Countries, Capitals and Representative Agriculture Cities
metadata.description: A continent-to-region-to-country directory with national capitals and one representative agriculture-oriented city, locality or agri-food district for each country where applicable.
metadata.continentOrderNote: The supplied list named six continents while calling it a seven-continent model. The six supplied items are retained in their original order and Africa is appended as the missing seventh continent.
metadata.countryScope: 193 United Nations member states plus the Holy See and the State of Palestine (195 total). Antarctica is represented as a continent with no sovereign countries.
metadata.regionalClassification: United Nations Statistics Division M49 geographic regions, adapted only in display labels where needed. Only sovereign states and the two UN non-member observer states are counted; dependent territories and separately administered areas are excluded.
classificationNotes: Russia is grouped in Europe, and Türkiye, Cyprus, Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia are grouped in Asia following the M49 geographic classification.
Mexico is grouped in Central America for this dataset because the M49 scheme places it there within the North America region.
Taiwan, Kosovo, Western Sahara and dependent territories are not counted as separate countries in the 195-country scope.
The Holy See is included as a UN non-member observer state; Vatican City is its capital city-state.
Some countries have multiple, disputed or de facto capital arrangements; these are explained in the capital string or country note rather than forced into a single simplistic answer.

agricultureCityMethodology.definition: A representative city or locality strongly associated with agricultural production, agricultural markets, agro-processing, agricultural research, or the farming region it serves.
agricultureCityMethodology.importantLimitation: There is no universally recognised official global ranking of the 'most farming city' for every country. City choices are curated representative associations, not a statistically proven first-place ranking.
selectionBasis: Prominence of surrounding crop, livestock, horticultural or plantation production
Role as a regional agricultural market, logistics, processing or service centre
Recognition as an agricultural research, university or agribusiness hub
For microstates with very limited agriculture, a notable farming locality or agri-food district is used where possible
agricultureCityMethodology.exceptions: Where there is no meaningful distinct farming city (for example, some highly urbanised or very small states), agricultureCity.name is null and the rationale states why. Where the useful reference is a district or farming area rather than a municipality, that is stated in the name and classification.
agricultureCityMethodology.sourceCaution: FAOSTAT and World Bank sources provide national-level agricultural context, not proof of the individual city choice. The city rationale is a curated synthesis and should be independently checked against national subnational statistics before being used for formal research or policy.

schema.continents: Array of continent objects in the declared order.
schema.regions: Array of subregion objects within each continent.
schema.countries: Array of country objects within each region.
schema.country.capital: Capital city or a transparent description of a multi-capital, transitional or de facto arrangement.
schema.country.agricultureCity: Object with name, classification, rationale, selection status, confidence and supporting national-agriculture context source IDs.
schema.sourceRegistry: Object mapping source IDs to source title, URL, supported claims and access date.

agricultureCity.rationale: Northern farming centre for cattle, maize and other dryland crops.

agricultureCity.name: Mbombela
agricultureCity.rationale: Mpumalanga centre serving subtropical fruit, citrus, nuts and sugarcane production.

antarcticaStatus.note: Antarctica is governed through the Antarctic Treaty System. Research stations are not sovereign states or national capitals.

UN_M49.title: United Nations Statistics Division — Standard country or area codes for statistical use (M49)
UN_M49.supports: Primary basis for continental and subregional grouping. M49 assigns each country or area to one region; this file uses its geographic logic with a sovereign-state scope and a few transparent presentation adjustments.

UN_MEMBER_STATES.title: United Nations — Member States
UN_MEMBER_STATES.supports: Reference for the 193 UN member states in the dataset's country-count baseline.

UN_OBSERVER_STATES.title: United Nations — Non-member observer states
UN_OBSERVER_STATES.supports: Reference for the Holy See and State of Palestine as the two non-member observer states included to create a commonly used 195-state scope.

FAOSTAT.title: FAO — FAOSTAT food and agriculture statistics
FAOSTAT.supports: National-level agriculture context (crop and livestock production, land use, inputs, trade and related indicators). FAOSTAT does not by itself prove that a particular city is the country's single leading farming city.

WORLD_BANK_AGRICULTURE.title: World Bank — Agriculture and Rural Development indicators
WORLD_BANK_AGRICULTURE.supports: Country-level agriculture context, including agricultural land, crop production, value added and employment indicators. Not a city-level ranking source.

UNGEGN_WORLD_GEOGRAPHICAL_NAMES.title: United Nations Group of Experts on Geographical Names — World Geographical Names database
UNGEGN_WORLD_GEOGRAPHICAL_NAMES.supports: Authoritative geographical names database for country names, capitals and major cities, using national names authorities where available. The cited UN 2025 documentation describes coverage of 193 UN member states and two observer states.

EQUATORIAL_GUINEA_CAPITAL_2026.title: Government of Equatorial Guinea — Decree-Law No. 1/2026 declaring Ciudad de la Paz the capital
EQUATORIAL_GUINEA_CAPITAL_2026.supports: Official 2 January 2026 decree establishing Ciudad de la Paz as the legal capital, with a one-year period for government institutions to relocate.

INDONESIA_CAPITAL_STATUS.title: Indonesia Constitutional Court — October 2026 decision confirms the Presidential Decree for capital transfer had not been issued
INDONESIA_CAPITAL_STATUS.supports: Current legal transition context for Indonesia: in its 29 October 2026 decision, the Constitutional Court discussed the absence of the required Presidential Decree and the continuing preparation for the transfer to Nusantara.

ANTARCTIC_TREATY.title: Antarctic Treaty Secretariat — The Antarctic Treaty
ANTARCTIC_TREATY.supports: International governance context; Antarctica is not a sovereign country and has no national capital.
